prompt: Once call centre agents were judged on call length, they started rushing customers off the phone.
tells: Once call centre agents were judged on call length
why: As soon as call length was measured and judged, people worked to the number instead of solving problems. Measuring changed behaviour.
trap: The system doesn't force short calls; the measure does.

prompt: Support staff began closing tickets early and reopening new ones to hit the target for tickets closed per day.
tells: to hit the target for tickets closed per day
why: The target made people chase the count rather than the help it stood for. A number changing how people work is the point.
trap: It looks like a workaround, but it's driven by the target, not a tool that doesn't fit.

prompt: After school funding was tied to test results, lessons narrowed to what the test covered.
tells: school funding was tied to test results
why: Once the number mattered for money, teaching bent toward it. What gets measured and rewarded changes what people do.
trap: Nothing is locked in by past choices; the measure itself steers behaviour.

prompt: When managers started counting lines of code written, programs suddenly got much longer.
tells: started counting lines of code written
why: Counting lines rewarded writing more lines, not better code. People work to the number once it's watched.
trap: The code isn't hidden; the change in behaviour came from the count.

prompt: Since the office started a step-count competition, people pace around during phone calls to hit 10,000 a day.
why: The visible count changed what people do during the day. That's measuring changing behaviour.
trap: The tracker doesn't open a new action; the target pushes them toward one.

prompt: Drivers learned that anything below five stars hurts them, so they ask every passenger directly for a five-star rating.
tells: anything below five stars hurts them
why: The rating number shapes how drivers behave with passengers. Measurement changing behaviour.
trap: Passengers aren't a gate drivers pass through; the score is what steers them.
